answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable bond before trading, with the bond recorded under a cipher-linked identity. Each honest deal adds a small ember of reputation that slowly raises the agent's credit limit, while any proven fraud burns the bond and pushes the agent off the ledge of trust, forcing a fresh, costly bond to re-enter. Duplicating identities therefore costs a new bond each time, so an attacker pays linearly per fake identity while honest agents amortise one bond over many deals.
